# AI Development Instructions

These instructions are the single source of truth for GitHub Copilot in VS Code and Copilot CLI.

## Feature Workflow

- `plan-motorcycle-web-app.md` at the repository root is the living document and holds only features (built) and tasks (what is left): Status, Features, Release Gates (G-nn), Tasks (T-nn), Done, Session log. Read it before starting work and update it when work ships; the production verdict changes only when every blocker gate is ticked with evidence. Keep it short: put architecture in `docs/architecture.md`, API in `docs/api.md`, schema in `docs/database.md`, decisions/targets in `docs/design-decisions.md`, and Azure resources, URLs, local dev and deployment troubleshooting in `docs/operations.md`, never in the plan. Feature `specs/` folders and the SpecKit workflow are no longer used; `.specify/` and `.github/skills/speckit-*` are kept only for possible future use, so do not invoke them unless asked.
- **End-of-day progress update.** When the user says to update the plan for progress (or similar), update the plan's **Tasks**: set each task's status (✅/🔄/⬜). Move finished tasks to the **Done** table with evidence. If a task is only partly done, mark it 🔄 and write what is left in its Notes, or split it into smaller tasks (keep tasks small; no phases or steps). Recompute the Progress counts, update the **Next up** line, add a dated entry at the top of the **Session log** (done, partly done, left off at, suggested next), and update affected gates. Only mark things done that were verified in code, tests, or user confirmation; do not guess.
- **Start-of-day "what next".** When the user asks what to do next, read the plan and answer from it: first list unfinished work from the latest Session log and any 🔄 tasks (with what is left), then offer the next ⬜ tasks as options (note gates). Keep it short and ask which to pick.
- Deliver backend and every affected frontend together. Update `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/api.md`, or `docs/database.md` when the corresponding contract, architecture, or schema changes.
- `apps/admin` is the private administration SPA. Do not add an alternate data path: both web applications must use the shared API.

## Commands

Run commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.

```powershell
# Install workspace dependencies
pnpm install
pnpm add <package> -w

# Public Next.js application
pnpm --filter web dev
pnpm --filter web build
pnpm --filter web lint
pnpm --filter web exec eslint app/page.tsx  # lint one file

# ASP.NET Core API
dotnet restore apps\api\Motorcycle.Api.slnx
dotnet build apps\api\Motorcycle.Api.slnx
dotnet test apps\api\Motorcycle.Api.slnx
dotnet run --project apps\api\Motorcycle.Api
dotnet ef database update --project apps\api\Motorcycle.Infrastructure --startup-project apps\api\Motorcycle.Api
dotnet ef migrations add <MigrationName> --project apps\api\Motorcycle.Infrastructure --startup-project apps\api\Motorcycle.Api
```

Use the shared API for both frontend applications. Do not add a separate data path for `apps/admin`; it is a private frontend and never connects directly to PostgreSQL or Azure Blob Storage.

The API targets .NET 10 and runs at `https://localhost:7240` from the single `https` launch profile. Visual Studio and `dotnet run --launch-profile https` use the same address. The public web app defaults to `https://localhost:7240` through `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. API unit tests live in `apps\api\Motorcycle.Api.Tests` (run `dotnet test apps\api\Motorcycle.Api.slnx`, or add `--filter <name>` for one test; stop a running API first or the build fails on locked DLLs). There are no frontend test runners yet.

## Next.js Version Guidance

The public app uses Next.js 16, whose APIs and conventions differ from earlier releases. Before changing Next.js code, read the relevant guide under `apps\web\node_modules\next\dist\docs\` and honor its deprecation notices. The `<!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->` block in `apps\web\AGENTS.md` is generated by `next dev`; do not remove it because it will be regenerated.

## Architecture

- This pnpm monorepo contains the public Next.js app in `apps/web`, a shared ASP.NET Core API in `apps/api`, and the private Vite React admin SPA in `apps/admin`. Both frontend applications use the shared API; neither may access PostgreSQL or Azure Blob Storage directly.
- The API follows Clean Architecture: `Motorcycle.Domain` holds entities, `Motorcycle.Application` owns DTOs, service contracts, repository contracts, and filtering contracts, `Motorcycle.Infrastructure` implements EF Core persistence, repositories, seeding, and filtering, and `Motorcycle.Api` contains controllers and dependency-injection composition.
- PostgreSQL stores flexible motorcycle specifications in the `bikes.specs` JSONB column. `spec_groups` and `spec_definitions` define display order, labels, units, and filter behavior; their `sortOrder` values must drive detail and comparison output. `MotorcycleDbContext` centrally maps EF Core database names to PostgreSQL snake_case.
- Controllers bind HTTP requests and delegate to Application services. Repositories load published catalog data with its related brand, category, and images; public catalog routes expose only published bikes.
- Public catalog endpoints are anonymous and read-only. Administration uses protected `/api/admin` endpoints with API-owned Facebook PKCE sign-in, an API-managed HttpOnly session, and active `AdminRole` authorization. Role, Brand, Category, BikeModel, Bike variant (including model reassignment, publication, reviewed flag), Azure Blob image, specification metadata, and bulk single-spec edit/grid mutations are implemented.

## Repository Conventions

- Use braces for every `if`/`else`, loop, and other control-flow body, even when it contains a single statement. Put the opening brace on the same line as the control statement, with the body and closing brace on separate lines. Keep this convention when editing existing code.
- Update the plan's Features, Tasks, and release gates, and the applicable `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/api.md`, or `docs/database.md`, with each implementation.
- Keep HTTP DTOs in `Motorcycle.Application` and mirror affected contracts in each frontend's TypeScript types. Frontend requests go through the application's centralized typed API client (`apps/web/lib/api.ts`); do not add component-level `fetch` calls.
- Register Application interfaces and Infrastructure implementations in `apps/api/Motorcycle.Api/Program.cs`. Controllers delegate to Application services rather than querying EF Core directly.
- Dynamic specification filtering is strategy-based. Add a new `ISpecFilterStrategy` implementation and register it in `Program.cs`; do not grow controller or service conditionals for new filter types.
- Preserve the JSONB spec model and the group/definition `sortOrder` ordering used by detail and comparison responses. Schema changes are EF Core migrations under `apps/api/Motorcycle.Infrastructure/Migrations`; keep PostgreSQL-specific indexes or SQL inside migrations.
- Database migrations run on every API startup, independently of configuration. `Database:MigrateOnStartup` (override with `Database__MigrateOnStartup`) retains its legacy name and controls only the development-only startup seed; its default is true in Development and false elsewhere. Production catalog data is managed through the protected admin API or the explicit seed command. Swagger UI is on in Development and elsewhere only with `Swagger__Enabled=true`.
- **Visual alignment (always):** `apps/admin` and `apps/web` must always look the same. Any styling or layout request (colors, fonts, spacing, sizes, header, sidebar, main/content area, borders, corners, shadows, buttons) targeting either app must be applied to both apps in the same change, in both directions (admin to web and web to admin), without the user asking for both. Only if the user explicitly says to change just one app, do that. Current shared conventions: full-width header (`min-h-16 px-6 py-4`) with the title at the far left and account/sign-out at the far right; sidebar `17.5rem` wide with each section as its own `bg-brand-sidebar p-4` card spaced `space-y-4`, gold `text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide` titles and `px-3 py-2 font-semibold` links; main content `bg-brand-content p-6 shadow-lg` inside `max-w-7xl p-4 md:p-8`; square corners (no `rounded-*`); Aptos / Segoe UI font. Keep the brand theme tokens identical in `apps/admin/src/styles.css` and `apps/web/app/globals.css`.
- Use the existing Tailwind theme tokens from `apps/web/app/globals.css` and mobile-first breakpoints. Remote motorcycle images use `next/image` and must match a `remotePatterns` entry in `apps/web/next.config.ts`.
- Do not put connection strings, API keys, or Blob Storage credentials in source. The API owns storage operations; Azure Key Vault and managed identity supply deployment secrets.
